title: Zoho Flow Free Plan: Limits, Trial, Alternatives
summary: Zoho Workflow free plan works as a real trial with feature limits.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits and where its free tier falls short


Activepieces gives you both routes: a free cloud plan with 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows, or the open-source edition running on your own server, and either is worth testing.


Its core is MIT-licensed (the LICENSE file in the GitHub repository says so, and puts the` packages/ee/` enterprise directories under a separate commercial licence).


Its 750 integrations are counted straight from the` packages/pieces/community` directory of that open-source monorepo, where **roughly 60% are community-contributed** , making broad ecosystem support come with decentralized maintenance, so each integration's sustainability depends on its maintainer's ongoing engagement.


It suits you if you can accept a smaller app catalog than Zapier's or Flow's Zoho depth in exchange.


### What the free tier gives you


Two ways in, one product: you can use Activepieces' hosted cloud, or you can run the open-source edition on your own server. That second route is what separates it from Flow, which exists only as Zoho's hosted service.


If your worry is a per-task meter, self-hosting changes the question. You stop buying runs from a vendor and start paying for a server and the time to keep it up.


Shown below, the cloud plans are laid out on its pricing page. It lists four tiers: Free at $0 a month, Plus at $25 a month and marked Recommended, Business at $150 a month, and Enterprise on custom pricing with a sales contact.


Before you trust the headline price, read each tier's own list, covering AI steps, active flows, AI credits, users and support, against your own workload, because the allowance that runs out first is different for each person.


Free costs nothing, and the first step up is $25 a month, so you can find out cheaply whether the limit you hit is one you can live with.


### Where it falls short of Zoho Workflow


Before you commit, know these four shortfalls.


Where one niche app in your stack has no[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) connector, you'll be building the integration through a generic HTTP step or writing it yourself. Zapier connects to far more apps.


For a stack centered on Zoho CRM and Zoho Books, Flow's free plan earns its place. Flow is built by Zoho, so its Zoho connectors are the deepest you'll find, and Activepieces' coverage of Zoho apps is thinner.


Self-hosting is your job: updates, backups, uptime and security fall to you. The software costs nothing, but the hours don't.


Caps apply on the free cloud tier too, set out on the pricing page. It's a trial of the product more than a permanent home for a busy workflow.


If your stack is mostly outside Zoho, those shortfalls are worth weighing against Flow's next plan. If it sits inside Zoho, stay on Flow.
